evals.prompt: I have a capability map at /home/z/my-project/capability-output/a6-domain-model.md from a legacy-capability-extractor run. It has 6 L1 capabilities with L2 sub-capabilities, descriptions, and actors. Convert all of them to Gherkin Feature files and save them to /home/z/my-project/features/.
evals.expected_output: Gherkin .feature files in /home/z/my-project/features/, one per L1 capability. Each Feature has the L1 capability name as title, the description and As-a/I-want/So-that narrative, a Background with shared preconditions, and at least one Scenario per L2 sub-capability (happy path). Scenarios use business language. Tags (@capability, @level1, @level2, per-L2 tag) are applied. Feature file syntax is valid.
expectations: One .feature file per L1 capability (6 features total)
Each Feature has the As-a / I-want / So-that narrative with a real business actor
Each Feature has a Background with shared preconditions
Each L2 capability has at least one Scenario, with happy-path scenarios for all
Scenarios use business language, not technical implementation details (no DB table names, class names, HTTP codes)
Tags @capability, @level1, @level2 and a per-L2 tag are applied consistently
Feature file syntax is valid (proper Given/When/Then indentation, colons after Feature/Scenario/Background)
Cross-capability dependencies from the input are reflected as Given preconditions linking to other Features
No composite scenarios exist — each Scenario tests a single operation or business rule
State-changing Scenarios end with verification And steps: audit log entry, response metadata

evals.prompt: Our project uses OpenSpec. The capability map is in /home/z/my-project/openspec/specs/domain-model.md. Convert the Customer Management and Order Processing L1 capabilities to Gherkin, create an OpenSpec change proposal, and place the feature files in the specs directory. Link the specs to tasks in tasks.md.
evals.expected_output: An OpenSpec proposal created with /opsx:propose containing two .feature files for Customer Management and Order Processing placed in the OpenSpec specs/ directory. The feature files have proper Feature/Scenario structure with business language. Tasks.md is updated with step-definition and test-data tasks. The proposal links back to the original domain model.
expectations: .feature files are placed in the OpenSpec specs/ directory
An OpenSpec proposal (/opsx:propose) is created linking the Gherkin specs
tasks.md is updated with implementation tasks (step definitions, test data)
The proposal references the original capability map for traceability
Feature files still follow all Gherkin conventions (narrative, Background, scenarios, tags)
Cross-capability dependency scenarios (e.g., Order Processing depends on Customer Management) are included
Every state-changing Scenario includes verification And steps (audit log, response metadata)

evals.prompt: Review the generated Gherkin files in /home/z/my-project/features/ for quality issues. The project had 6 L1 capabilities with 18 total L2 sub-capabilities. Check for anti-patterns: technical language in scenarios, missing actors or business value, duplicate scenarios, composite scenarios testing multiple operations, missing verification steps, and L2 capabilities with no scenarios. Write findings to /home/z/my-project/gherkin-review.md.
evals.expected_output: A review document mapping findings to the skill's anti-patterns. Identifies any scenarios with technical jargon (DB names, class names, HTTP codes), Features missing the As-a/I-want/So-that narrative, duplicate scenarios across Feature files, composite scenarios testing multiple operations in one Scenario, state-changing Scenarios missing verification And steps, and any L2 capability from the original map that lacks a corresponding Scenario. Each finding includes the file, line number, anti-pattern category, and remediation step.
expectations: Flags any scenario steps that use technical implementation details instead of business language
Flags any Feature missing the As-a / I-want / So-that narrative
Identifies duplicate scenarios across Feature files
Identifies composite Scenarios that test multiple operations (should be split)
Identifies state-changing Scenarios missing verification And steps (audit, metadata)
Cross-references the original capability map to find L2 capabilities with no Scenario
Each finding includes file path, line number, anti-pattern category, and a concrete remediation step
Review output is formatted as findings mapped to the skill's anti-pattern categories

evals.prompt: The capability map shows 10 cross-capability dependency relationships across 6 L1 capabilities but only 2 cross-capability Scenarios were generated. Review the generated Gherkin files in /home/z/my-project/features/, identify the missing dependency edges, and generate the missing @cross-capability Scenarios for all 10 relationships.
evals.expected_output: Updated .feature files with @cross-capability Scenarios for all 10 dependency edges. Each missing Scenario references the dependent capability in its Given preconditions, tests the dependency interaction, and ends with relevant verification steps. A report lists all 10 edges and confirms each has a corresponding Scenario.
expectations: Every dependency edge in the capability map's cross-capability section has a corresponding @cross-capability Scenario
Each @cross-capability Scenario references the dependent capability in its Given preconditions
Each @cross-capability Scenario has the @cross-capability tag
Cross-capability Scenarios end with cascade-effect and audit-log verification And steps
A summary report confirms all 10 dependency edges are covered

evals.prompt: A rate-limiting capability has only one Scenario testing rate limit behavior. Convert it to use Scenario Outline with Examples tables covering at least 4 distinct data values (within-limit, at-limit, one-over-limit, way-over-limit). Add a similar Scenario Outline for file upload media type acceptance (image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf accepted; application/exe, text/html rejected).
evals.expected_output: Two Scenario Outlines: one for rate limits with 4+ Examples rows and one for media types with 5+ Examples rows. Both use <angle-bracket> placeholders matching the Examples column names. Each row independently verifies the expected behavior. Response metadata checks confirm headers are present.
expectations: Rate limit Scenario Outline has at least 4 Examples rows (within-limit, at-limit, over-limit, way-over-limit)
Media type Scenario Outline has at least 5 Examples rows covering accepted and rejected types
Both use Scenario Outline with Examples table and <angle-bracket> placeholders
Each row independently tests the expected behavior
Both include response metadata verification And steps
